prompt.brief: Design a Pastebin-like service where users create text pastes, receive short URLs, optionally protect or expire them, and read them reliably at internet scale.
successSignals: Separate immutable paste content from mutable metadata, abuse controls, and read caching.
Choose an ID strategy that is compact, non-sequential to users, and safe under retries.
Use object or blob storage and a CDN for popular reads while keeping the write path durable.
Explain expiration, privacy, abuse prevention, deletion, and cache invalidation.

functional: Create a paste from text and return a short, shareable identifier.
Read a paste by identifier with optional syntax highlighting and raw-content access.
Support public, unlisted, and password-protected pastes with optional expiration.
Allow owners and moderators to delete content, report abuse, and audit administrative actions.
nonFunctional: A successful create must durably retain the paste before its URL is returned.
Target p95 below 100 ms for a cache hit and below 300 ms for a metadata-backed read.
Reads should scale independently from writes and tolerate hot pastes without database overload.
Expired or deleted content must stop being served even when edge and application caches are warm.
scaleAssumptions: 20 million new pastes per day, 2 billion reads per day, and 50,000 peak read requests per second.
Most pastes are small text blobs, but a strict size limit prevents oversized uploads from becoming a storage path.
A small fraction of links become extremely hot after being shared publicly.
Retention varies from minutes to permanent; expired content is deleted or moved to a cold tier by policy.

metrics.label: Paste create rate
metrics.description: 20M creates per day with burst capacity for campaigns.

metrics.label: Read latency
metrics.description: Popular immutable content should be served from edge or regional cache.

metrics.label: Cache hit rate
metrics.description: Track hit rate by region and evict on deletion or policy changes.

metrics.label: Expiry accuracy
metrics.description: The serving path checks expiry and deletion state, not only cache TTL.

entities.name: Paste
entities.notes: Metadata is the authority; immutable content is stored separately under a versioned key.

entities.name: PasteContent
entities.notes: Store the body as immutable data so retries and cache reads are safe.

entities.name: RateLimitBucket
entities.notes: Apply separate limits by account, IP, token, and destination risk.

entities.name: Report
entities.notes: Reports enter a moderation queue and do not directly mutate content without policy checks.

entities.name: AuditEvent
entities.notes: Append-only security evidence for deletes, password changes, and moderator actions.

apis.contract: { body, language, visibility, password, expiresIn, requestId } -> { pasteId, url, expiresAt }
apis.notes: Validate size and policy, write content and metadata idempotently, then return the identifier.

apis.contract: { password? } -> { pasteId, body, language, createdAt, expiresAt }
apis.notes: Check state, expiry, and password authorization before returning content or a cacheable response.
Use a streaming response and content-disposition rules to prevent unsafe browser interpretation.
Authorize the owner or moderator, write a tombstone, and publish invalidation work.
Rate-limit reports and enqueue review without exposing reporter identity.

dataFlow.title: Validate and reserve the paste
dataFlow.description: The gateway authenticates the caller, applies abuse and size limits, normalizes language metadata, and creates an idempotency record.

dataFlow.title: Commit immutable content
dataFlow.description: The service writes the body under a content key and commits the metadata record only after storage confirms the checksum.

dataFlow.title: Return the short URL
dataFlow.description: A collision-safe ID generator allocates the paste ID; the response is returned only after the durable transaction succeeds.

dataFlow.title: Serve through cache
dataFlow.description: Reads check authorization and lifecycle state, then fetch immutable content from regional cache, CDN, or blob storage.

dataFlow.title: Invalidate and expire asynchronously
dataFlow.description: Delete, moderation, and expiry events purge caches, tombstone metadata, remove blobs, and feed audit and analytics consumers.

architecture.title: Pastebin reference architecture
architecture.summary: A small durable metadata service controls immutable paste bodies, while cache and CDN layers absorb read traffic and event workers handle lifecycle and moderation.

layers.label: Edge and API
layers.description: Clients, rate limits, authentication, and cacheable read responses.

layers.label: Source data
layers.description: Paste metadata, ownership, lifecycle, and content storage.

layers.label: Asynchronous lifecycle
layers.description: Durable events drive invalidation, expiry, moderation, and analytics.

keyPaths.label: Create paste
keyPaths.description: Client -> gateway -> paste service -> blob and metadata stores -> response.

keyPaths.label: Read paste
keyPaths.description: Client -> CDN or cache -> authorization-aware service -> immutable content.

keyPaths.label: Delete or expire
keyPaths.description: Source mutation -> event stream -> purge, tombstone, moderation, and audit consumers.

deepDives.title: Short ID generation
points: Use random or time-sortable IDs encoded in a URL-safe alphabet.
Reserve IDs with conditional writes so retries cannot create duplicate mappings.
Do not expose sequential database keys that enable enumeration.

deepDives.title: Caching private content
points: Never share password-protected responses across users without a safe authorization-aware key.
Cache public immutable bodies aggressively but keep lifecycle state authoritative.
Purge by paste ID and version when moderation or deletion changes access.

deepDives.title: Expiration and deletion
points: Check expires_at and state before every serve, including cache revalidation.
Write a tombstone first, then asynchronously purge caches and blobs.
Use a due-time index plus periodic sweeps to repair missed expiry events.

deepDives.title: Abuse controls
points: Limit create rate, body size, suspicious destinations, and repeated reads by risk score.
Scan links and content asynchronously, with quarantine available before public indexing.
Keep moderation and audit paths independent from the hot read path.

tradeoffs.title: Database body versus blob storage
tradeoffs.recommendation: Keep metadata in a low-latency database and bodies in immutable blob storage.
tradeoffs.caution: The two-step write needs a pending state and repair worker.

tradeoffs.title: Random versus sequential IDs
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use random, compact IDs to reduce enumeration and hot partitions.
tradeoffs.caution: Random IDs need collision handling and may be less index-friendly.

tradeoffs.title: Cache TTL versus purge
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use both short lifecycle-aware TTLs and explicit purge events.
tradeoffs.caution: Purge is at-least-once, so the origin must still reject deleted content.

commonMistakes: Returning a URL before the paste body and metadata are durable.
Using predictable sequential IDs that make enumeration trivial.
Caching password-protected responses under only the paste ID.
Relying exclusively on cache expiry for deletes and expiration.
Allowing unbounded paste size or create rate without abuse controls.

followUps.question: How do you handle a paste that suddenly goes viral?
followUps.answer: Promote its immutable public response to CDN and regional caches, use request coalescing on misses, and protect the origin with per-key limits.

followUps.question: What if blob storage succeeds but metadata commit fails?
followUps.answer: Keep the object under a pending key, retry the metadata transaction idempotently, and garbage-collect abandoned objects after a safety window.

followUps.question: How do you prevent deleted content from remaining at the edge?
followUps.answer: Write the tombstone first, publish purge events, use short revalidation windows, and make the origin return a hard denial for deleted IDs.

followUps.question: How would you support permanent pastes?
followUps.answer: Use an explicit retention class, legal and abuse takedown overrides, and lifecycle policies that preserve the body while metadata remains authoritative.

rubric.description: The design commits paste metadata and immutable content safely before returning a URL.
The design uses CDN or cache layers, hot-key protection, and independent read scaling.
Expiration, deletion, tombstones, invalidation, and repair work are explicit.
Authentication, password handling, enumeration resistance, quotas, moderation, and auditability are covered.
